answer: Semantic Similarity Slashing: agents whose submissions cluster too tightly are flagged, then mutually slash bonded stake. Each identity must post a marble-hard bond; similarity above threshold triggers an ember of doubt that burns both stakes. Underwriting the opal of reputation means honest agents stay dispersed. A farmer cloning k answers needs k distinct bonds, so cost scales linearly while detectable clusters lose everything. Works because collusion leaves fingerprints cheap to spot but expensive to fake.
